hosts.name: S3-compatible bucket, user-owned (AWS S3 / Cloudflare R2 / Backblaze B2 / MinIO) — RECOMMENDED primary 'bring your own bucket' host
hosts.auth: User pastes: endpoint URL, region, access key id, secret key, bucket name, public base URL. Client signs requests itself with AWS SigV4 (no server). Two modes: (a) direct signed PUT with Authorization header, or (b) generate a presigned PUT URL locally and PUT to it (same thing, useful if upload is delegated to a background isolate/native uploader). VERIFIED (AWS docs, PresignedUrlUploadObject): presigned URL expiry can be set up to 7 days with IAM user keys; if Content-Type is included in the signature the upload must send the identical Content-Type or SignatureDoesNotMatch; clock skew also causes SignatureDoesNotMatch. VERIFIED (R2 presigned-urls doc): R2 supports presigned GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE, SigV4, min 1s / max 7 days (604,800s), only on https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com (not on custom domains); browser-form POST presign is not supported. VERIFIED (B2 S3-compatible API doc): presigned URLs supported, object-level ACLs NOT supported (bucket-level only), browser-based POST to presigned URL not supported, no IAM roles. VERIFIED (MinIO mc docs): `mc anonymous set download ALIAS/BUCKET` makes a bucket publicly readable.
hosts.direct_link: Bucket must be PUBLIC-READ (per-bucket setting), then the GET URL carries no query string and no redirect: AWS: https://{bucket}.s3.{region}.amazonaws.com/{key} (bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject, Block Public Access off); R2: https://pub-<hash>.r2.dev/{key} (VERIFIED: 'rate-limited and should only be used for development purposes', 'intended for non-production traffic') or a custom domain on a Cloudflare zone (recommended; adds cache/WAF); B2: https://{bucket}.s3.{region}.backblazeb2.com/{key} (VERIFIED, doc calls it 'easiest to use') or friendly URL https://f00x.backblazeb2.com/file/{bucket}/{key}; MinIO: https://{host}/{bucket}/{key} after `mc anonymous set download`. Alternative WITHOUT a public bucket: a presigned GET URL (query-string SigV4, ≤7 days). Meta only documents 'must be on a public server' and community reports (n8n thread 2025-08-11, postpeer error 2207052) say signed URLs with short TTL fail at fetch time, not that query strings are forbidden; presigned GET is therefore 'probably works but risky' — recommend public-read + Content-Type set on PUT. The object's Content-Type is what you send in the PUT (all four honor it); always send image/jpeg, image/png or video/mp4.
hosts.limits: AWS S3: no free tier for this purpose beyond 12-month trial (unverified, not fetched); single PUT up to 5 GB (unverified). Cloudflare R2 (VERIFIED pricing page, 2026-10): free 10 GB-month storage, 1M Class A ops/month (PUT/DELETE-list), 10M Class B ops/month (GET), egress free incl. r2.dev; free tier only for Standard storage class. VERIFIED (R2 get-started): creating a bucket requires completing an 'R2 subscription' checkout; community posts (2025-11, 2026) say a payment method must be on file even for free tier. Backblaze B2 (VERIFIED pricing, 2026-10): first 10 GB always free, free egress up to 3x average monthly storage then $0.01/GB, free unlimited egress to Cloudflare/Fastly CDNs, Class A/B/C API calls free, Class D 2,500/day free. MinIO: self-hosted, unlimited; user must expose it on public HTTPS. Presigned-URL max validity 7 days on AWS and R2.
hosts.deletion: S3 DELETE Object with SigV4 (`DELETE /{key}`), or presigned DELETE (R2 supports presign DELETE; AWS too). Optionally set a bucket lifecycle rule 'expire after 1 day' as a safety net (AWS, R2 and B2 all support lifecycle rules — unverified for B2 exact UI). Crier can delete immediately after the container reaches FINISHED/PUBLISHED (see meta_requirements) but should keep the object for Threads/IG video until status_code=PUBLISHED and for TikTok until publish status is PUBLISH_COMPLETE (TikTok says URL must stay reachable for the whole download, which times out 1 h after start).
hosts.tos_fit: Best fit: user's own paid/free account, no third-party ToS problem, no abuse angle, no account-ban risk. Only caveat: r2.dev is explicitly dev-only/rate-limited; B2 and AWS public URLs are fine for production.
hosts.dart_notes: Packages: `aws_signature_v4` (pub.dev, publisher aws-amplify.com, v0.6.13 ~2026-08, all platforms) — VERIFIED has `AWSSigV4Signer.sign/signSync` and `presign/presignSync(request, credentialScope: AWSCredentialScope(region, service: AWSService.s3), expiresIn: Duration, serviceConfiguration: S3ServiceConfiguration(signPayload: false))`; S3ServiceConfiguration exposes unsignedPayloadHash (x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD) which is what you want for large files and for R2/B2. `minio` (xtyxtyx/minio-dart, v3.5.8, ~2025-09, MIT, unofficial) — VERIFIED has putObject, removeObject, presignedPutObject, presignedGetObject and works with any S3-compatible endpoint; simplest drop-in. `aws_s3_api` (agilord, v2.0.0, 3 years old) — generated client, stale, avoid. Implementation: keep a MediaHost interface {Future<Uri> upload(File, contentType), Future<void> delete(Uri)}; for S3 build the PUT manually: PUT https://{endpoint}/{bucket}/{key} with headers Host, x-amz-date, x-amz-content-sha256 (UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD or sha256 of file), Content-Type, Content-Length; sign with region+service 's3' (R2 uses region 'auto', B2 uses e.g. 'us-west-004', MinIO 'us-east-1'). Use path-style (`/bucket/key`) for MinIO and R2, virtual-host style works on AWS/B2. Store secrets in flutter_secure_storage. Validate config on save by PUT+GET+DELETE of a 1-byte probe object and by HEAD on the public URL checking HTTP 200 and Content-Type.

hosts.name: Nextcloud / ownCloud (WebDAV + OCS public share link)
hosts.auth: User supplies server URL + login name + app password (Nextcloud 'Login flow v2' or manually created app password; HTTP Basic). Upload: PUT https://{host}/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/{path} (WebDAV, Basic auth). Share: POST https://{host}/ocs/v2.php/apps/files_sharing/api/v1/shares with header `OCS-APIRequest: true`, form fields path, shareType=3 (public link), permissions=1 (read), optional password, expireDate=YYYY-MM-DD; response (XML, or JSON with ?format=json) contains share `id`, `token`, `url`. VERIFIED from OCS Share API docs.
hosts.direct_link: Share page https://{host}/s/{token} returns an HTML page (not usable). Append /download: https://{host}/s/{token}/download — VERIFIED via Nextcloud forum that this is the documented community pattern and returns the file bytes; however a 2026-02 forum thread (NC 32.0.5) and a 2025-09 thread (NC 31.0.7–31.0.9) report that newer versions rewrite /download to https://{host}/public.php/dav/files/{token}/ which serves the bytes with Content-Disposition: attachment and strict CSP headers, and the preview endpoint /s/{token}/preview returned 404 on NC 32. Whether Meta/TikTok accept a 200 + attachment response is untested; the public.php/dav URL can also 500 on password-protected shares without a session. The community 'raw' app (https://{host}/apps/raw/s/{token}) serves the raw file with proper MIME (apps.nextcloud.com page could not be fetched — version support unverified). Treat Nextcloud as 'works on many instances, verify with a HEAD/GET probe that the final URL answers 200 with the right Content-Type and no 3xx'; prefer public.php/dav/files/{token}/ or /apps/raw/s/{token} over /s/{token}/download.
hosts.limits: Server-defined (PHP upload_max_filesize/chunking); Nextcloud chunked upload exists for large files (unverified detail). No fee. Shares can carry expireDate and password (password-protected shares are useless here).
hosts.deletion: DELETE https://{host}/ocs/v2.php/apps/files_sharing/api/v1/shares/{share_id} (status 100 = ok, VERIFIED) then WebDAV DELETE https://{host}/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/{path}. Or set expireDate = tomorrow on creation as a safety net.
hosts.tos_fit: User's own server: perfect ToS fit (self-hosted, AGPL). Not an 'abuse' route. Weakness is purely technical (direct-link behaviour drifts between Nextcloud versions).
hosts.dart_notes: `nextcloud` (pub.dev v9.0.0, ~2026-04, AGPL-3.0 — license is viral; fine for a GPL app) covers WebDAV + files_sharing OCS with app-password Bearer/Basic auth. `webdav_client` (v1.2.2, 2 years stale, Basic/Digest, writeFromFile, remove) is a lighter option. Or just use `dio`/`http`: PUT with Basic auth header, then POST OCS form with ?format=json and parse ocs.data.token. Always run the reachability probe (GET final URL, expect 200, no redirect, Content-Type starts with image/ or video/) before handing the URL to Meta.

hosts.name: GitHub Releases / GitHub Pages / raw.githubusercontent.com
hosts.auth: GitHub PAT (fine-grained, contents:write) → POST https://uploads.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{id}/assets?name=x.jpg with Content-Type header (release asset upload, unverified exact doc fetch); Pages requires a commit + build (10 builds/hour soft limit, VERIFIED).
hosts.direct_link: Release asset browser_download_url https://github.com/{o}/{r}/releases/download/{tag}/{name} — this URL 302-redirects to objects.githubusercontent.com (well known behaviour; unverified by fetch), which VIOLATES TikTok's 'HTTP 3xx is invalid' rule and is risky for Meta. raw.githubusercontent.com serves files directly with Content-Type but is for repository content. GitHub Pages serves direct 200 with correct MIME at https://{user}.github.io/{repo}/{file} but needs a build cycle (minutes).
hosts.limits: VERIFIED: each release asset < 2 GiB, up to 1000 assets per release, 'no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage'. Pages: 1 GB site, 100 GB/month soft bandwidth, 10 builds/hour.
hosts.deletion: DELETE /repos/{o}/{r}/releases/assets/{id} via API (unverified fetch). Pages requires another commit.
hosts.tos_fit: POOR. VERIFIED AUP: 'If we determine your bandwidth usage to be significantly excessive ... we reserve the right to suspend your Account, throttle your file hosting'. VERIFIED Pages terms: not allowed as free hosting for business/commercial content; Codespaces terms literally say 'don't use ... as a content delivery network'. GitHub staff/community guidance (search result) says GitHub is not a CDN for images/video. Using a repo as a throwaway media relay is exactly that. Do NOT ship as a default; at most an 'advanced, your-own-risk' option, and the redirect on release assets breaks TikTok anyway.
hosts.dart_notes: Not recommended; if implemented, use `http` with Bearer PAT, and probe the final URL for 3xx before use (expect failure for TikTok).

hosts.name: Catbox.moe (permanent) and Litterbox (temporary) — free anonymous hosts
hosts.auth: Catbox: POST https://catbox.moe/user/api.php multipart: reqtype=fileupload, fileToUpload=@file, optional userhash=<account hash> (anonymous allowed). Litterbox: POST https://litterbox.catbox.moe/resources/internals/api.php multipart: reqtype=fileupload, time=1h|12h|24h|72h, fileToUpload=@file; litterbox is anonymous-only. VERIFIED from tools pages. Response body is the plain-text URL (community-known; not stated on the page — treat as verified-by-convention).
hosts.direct_link: https://files.catbox.moe/{id}.{ext} and https://litter.catbox.moe/{id}.{ext} — direct file, extension preserved, served with the file's MIME (file is a 1-to-1 copy per FAQ). No redirect. Unverified by HEAD probe in this session.
hosts.limits: Catbox: 200 MB per file (VERIFIED home page); .gif over 20 MB rejected; banned extensions .exe .scr .cpl .doc* .jar; anonymous files kept until 2 years of inactivity, account files permanent (VERIFIED FAQ). Litterbox: 1 GB per file, expiry 1 h / 12 h / 24 h / 72 h (VERIFIED). No documented rate limits.
hosts.deletion: Catbox: reqtype=deletefiles with userhash and files=<space-separated names> — requires an account userhash (anonymous uploads cannot be deleted via API, VERIFIED field list implies userhash). Litterbox: no deletion; expires by `time` (use 1h for Meta, 12h/24h for TikTok video).
hosts.tos_fit: MIXED. VERIFIED FAQ: 'commercial use' via hotlinking, CDNs and monetised sites prohibited; 'Catbox will not engage in commercial use with third party organizations without prior approval' (legal page). A GPL hobby app where the user uploads their own creation and Meta fetches it once is arguably the permitted 'distribute your creations' case, but automated-tool use is unaddressed. Litterbox with 1 h expiry is the most defensible: the file is fetched once by Meta then vanishes. Content restrictions (no full episodes, gore, etc.) apply. Operator is a single volunteer; availability is best-effort.
hosts.dart_notes: Trivial with `http.MultipartRequest`; set a descriptive User-Agent ('Crier/x.y (+repo url)'). Response is the bare URL string; treat any non-https body as an error. Recommend Litterbox 1h as the zero-config default for images; warn that 1 GB/72 h videos should use 24h. Verify the URL with a HEAD before container creation (Content-Type is derived from extension on their side).

hosts.name: 0x0.st (The Null Pointer) — free anonymous host
hosts.auth: Anonymous: POST https://0x0.st multipart `file=@...` (also `url=` remote fetch, `expires=` hours-or-epoch-ms, `secret=` for unguessable URL). Response is the plain-text URL. Server also returns an `X-Token` header; later POST to the file URL with `token=...&delete=` deletes, `token=...&expires=` changes expiry. [RECALLED, NOT VERIFIED: 0x0.st and git.0x0.st did not resolve from this environment, GitHub mirror README 404'd; only blog posts (lalitm.com 2025-10-25, tuananh.net 2024-12-26) confirming 'curl -F file=@ https://0x0.st' and '30 days to 1 year by size' were readable.]
hosts.direct_link: https://0x0.st/{id}.{ext} direct, served with the sniffed MIME type, no redirect [recalled].
hosts.limits: [recalled] 512 MiB max; retention = min 30 days, max 365 days, scaled down with file size; blocked MIME blacklist incl. executables; service blocks some generic user agents and expects a meaningful User-Agent [recalled, uncertain].
hosts.deletion: [recalled] POST to the file URL with form fields token=<X-Token> and delete= (or expires=<ms epoch>). This makes 0x0 the only free anonymous host with per-file deletion without an account.
hosts.tos_fit: [recalled] Terms forbid malware, piracy, doxxing, CSAM, and 'spam'/abusive automation; personal use of your own media is within intent. Operator is a single person; no SLA. Because the terms could not be fetched today, ship only behind an 'I have read https://0x0.st terms' toggle and re-verify the terms page before release.
hosts.dart_notes: http.MultipartRequest, read `response.headers['x-token']` and persist it alongside the URL so Crier can delete right after publish. Set explicit User-Agent.

hosts.name: Uguu.se (Pomf-style) — free anonymous host
hosts.auth: Anonymous: POST https://uguu.se/upload multipart field `files[]`; `?output=json|text|csv|html|gyazo`, JSON default (VERIFIED api page). JSON shape [recalled from Uguu source]: {"success":true,"files":[{"hash","name","url","size"}]}.
hosts.limits: 128 MiB max, files expire after 3 hours (VERIFIED). Server-side upload rate limiting exists (VERIFIED README feature list).
hosts.tos_fit: VERIFIED FAQ: anything legal in Germany/Sweden/France that you have the right to publish; malware removed. No commercial-use or hotlink clause. 3 h lifetime fits the 'fetch once' pattern well for images; 128 MiB rules out most videos. Operated by Pomf AB (Sweden). Software is GPL-3.0 so Crier could also point at any self-hosted Uguu instance (configurable base URL).
hosts.dart_notes: MultipartRequest with field name exactly 'files[]'; parse files[0].url. Expose 'instance URL' so self-hosters can use their own Uguu.

hosts.name: Imgur API
hosts.auth: POST https://api.imgur.com/3/image (or /3/upload) with header `Authorization: Client-ID {id}`, multipart image=/video=, returns data.link and data.deletehash [recalled]. BLOCKER (VERIFIED 2025-12-11 Tautulli issue #2620, phpBB support thread, imguruploader.com article): Imgur no longer accepts new API application registrations — api.imgur.com/oauth2/addclient redirects to the homepage and support says no timeline. A new FOSS app cannot obtain its own Client-ID; users cannot register one either. Existing Client-IDs reportedly still work. Also Imgur's 2023 ToS changes removed anonymous (not-logged-in) uploads from the website, and the API ToS forbids commercial use without approval [recalled].
hosts.direct_link: https://i.imgur.com/{id}.jpg direct, no redirect [recalled]. Imgur re-encodes/strips metadata and may convert; not a 1:1 copy.
hosts.limits: [recalled] 10 MB images (20 MB on some paths), 200 MB video / 60 s; ~1,250 uploads/day per Client-ID, 12,500 requests/day; images not linked to an account have historically been purged if unviewed for months.
hosts.tos_fit: Not viable in 2026: no new app registration, anonymous web uploads already removed in 2023, API ToS non-commercial only. Do not implement.

hosts.name: Cloudinary (free plan, unsigned upload preset)
hosts.auth: User creates a free account (no card), creates an UNSIGNED upload preset, enters cloud_name + preset in Crier. Upload: POST https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/{cloud_name}/image/upload (or /video/upload or /auto/upload) multipart file=@, upload_preset=..., optional public_id, return_delete_token=true. VERIFIED: unsigned uploads need no API secret; signed uploads use SHA-1(params sorted + api_secret) and a signature valid 1 hour. Files > 100 MB must use chunked upload.
hosts.direct_link: https://res.cloudinary.com/{cloud_name}/image/upload/{public_id}.jpg (or /video/upload/...). VERIFIED format; version segment optional. Served from CDN with correct Content-Type, direct 200. Cloudinary can also transcode (f_jpg) which helps meet Meta's JPEG-only rule.
hosts.limits: VERIFIED (compare-plans, 2026-10): Free plan max 10 MB per image, 100 MB per video, 10 MB raw; Admin API 500 req/hour; 25 monthly credits (1 credit = 1,000 transformations or 1 GB storage or 1 GB bandwidth), 3 users/1 account, no credit card. 100 MB video cap is below Threads' 1 GB and TikTok's 4 GB.
hosts.deletion: With return_delete_token=true the response includes delete_token usable for 10 minutes via POST https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/{cloud}/delete_by_token (VERIFIED 10-minute window). Beyond that you need api_key+api_secret for /image/destroy (signed) or the Admin API. Practical: delete immediately after the container reaches FINISHED (usually < 1 min), or let the user also paste API key/secret for guaranteed cleanup.
hosts.tos_fit: Good: user's own account, product is built for exactly this (media delivery to third parties); free tier is intended for devs/hobbyists. 10 MB image limit is above Instagram's 8 MB and Threads' 8 MB, so images fit; videos constrained.
hosts.dart_notes: `cloudinary_public` (djade.net, v0.23.1, 2 years old, unsigned preset uploads, Android/iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux) exists but a raw `http.MultipartRequest` is 20 lines and avoids the stale dependency. If you add signed mode, signature = SHA1 of 'public_id=...&timestamp=...' + api_secret (use `crypto` package).

hosts.name: Supabase Storage (free plan, public bucket)
hosts.auth: User creates a free project, a PUBLIC bucket, and RLS policies on storage.objects allowing INSERT/DELETE for the chosen role; Crier gets project URL + anon key (or a service_role key, which bypasses RLS — simpler but powerful; keep in secure storage). Upload: POST https://{ref}.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/{bucket}/{path} with headers apikey: {key}, Authorization: Bearer {key}, Content-Type: image/jpeg, body = bytes (VERIFIED endpoint/headers). TUS resumable upload recommended > 6 MB (VERIFIED).
hosts.direct_link: https://{ref}.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/{bucket}/{path} — VERIFIED format; direct 200, Content-Type taken from the upload header. Signed URLs also exist (/object/sign/...) but carry a token query string.
hosts.limits: VERIFIED pricing/file-limits (2026-10): Free = 1 GB storage, 5 GB egress + 5 GB cached egress, max file upload 50 MB (global limit 'can't exceed 50 MB' on Free; Pro up to 500 GB), 2 active projects, projects PAUSED after 1 week of inactivity (a paused project makes the URL dead until the user un-pauses — bad for occasional posters).
hosts.deletion: DELETE https://{ref}.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/{bucket} with JSON body {"prefixes":["path"]} (VERIFIED REST equivalent of storage.from().remove()).
hosts.tos_fit: Acceptable (user's own project), but the 1-week auto-pause and the RLS setup burden (community reports of dashboard-created policies not applying to anon INSERT; must write SQL) make it a poor default for non-technical users. 50 MB cap excludes larger videos.
hosts.dart_notes: `supabase_flutter` v2.18.0 (supabase.io verified, 2026-09) has storage.from(b).uploadBinary(path, bytes, fileOptions: FileOptions(contentType:)), getPublicUrl(path) and remove([...]). Using raw `http` keeps the dependency tree small; the anon key must be sent in both apikey and Authorization headers.

hosts.name: Self-hosted 'Crier relay' (Cloudflare Worker + R2 binding; alternatively Deno Deploy)
hosts.auth: User deploys a ~60-line Worker (one `wrangler deploy` or dashboard paste) with an R2 bucket binding and a secret UPLOAD_TOKEN. Crier does PUT https://relay.example.workers.dev/u/{uuid}.{ext} with `Authorization: Bearer {token}` and Content-Type; Worker does `env.BUCKET.put(key, request.body, {httpMetadata:{contentType}})` (VERIFIED R2 Workers API: put(key, value, options) with httpMetadata.contentType; get() returns R2ObjectBody with writeHttpMetadata(headers); delete(key|keys[]) up to 1000 keys). GET /u/{key} is unauthenticated and streams the object with the stored Content-Type; DELETE /u/{key} requires the token. Add `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and optionally serve from a custom domain to avoid r2.dev limits (the Worker URL itself is not r2.dev-rate-limited).
hosts.direct_link: https://{name}.{account}.workers.dev/u/{uuid}.jpg (or custom domain) — direct 200, no redirect, exact Content-Type, no query string. This is the cleanest URL shape of all options and the only free one where a TikTok 'URL prefix' (https://relay.../u/) can be verified by hosting TikTok's signature file at that prefix (VERIFIED TikTok verification methods: domain via DNS record or URL-prefix via downloaded signature file served under the prefix).
hosts.limits: Workers Free (VERIFIED limits page): 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU per request (streaming to R2 is I/O, fine), 100 MB max request body on Free (so videos > 100 MB need multipart/R2 presign path or paid plan, which raises body limit to 200–500 MB), 50 subrequests/request. R2 Free: 10 GB-month, 1M Class A, 10M Class B, free egress; payment method must be on file to enable R2 (VERIFIED checkout step). Deno Deploy Free (VERIFIED pricing 2026-10): 1M requests/month, 20 GiB egress, 10 CPU-hours, 5 custom domains, but Deno Deploy has no bundled object store, so it would still need an S3 bucket — Workers+R2 is the better single-vendor relay.
hosts.deletion: DELETE /u/{key} → env.BUCKET.delete(key). Also attach an R2 lifecycle rule 'delete after 1 day' so nothing leaks if Crier crashes mid-publish. Optionally a scheduled Worker (cron) that lists and deletes objects older than 24 h.
hosts.tos_fit: Excellent: user's own Cloudflare account, no third-party content policy beyond Cloudflare's normal terms; no abuse concerns; private by default (unguessable UUID keys). Cost: zero within free tier. Only friction is the one-time deploy and the payment-method-on-file for R2.
hosts.dart_notes: Ship the Worker source in the repo (`relay/worker.js` + wrangler.toml) and a 'Deploy to Cloudflare' button link. In Dart it is a plain `http.put` with Bearer header and bytes/stream body; parse the returned JSON {url}. Because the relay is the recommended TikTok PULL_FROM_URL target, also ship an endpoint `GET /tiktok{whatever}.txt` that serves the user-pasted TikTok verification file content (store it as a Worker secret/KV) so URL-prefix verification works.

meta_requirements: VERIFIED (Instagram Content Publishing doc, IG User Media reference, Threads Posts doc, all read 2026-10-07): Meta fetches the file server-side — 'We cURL media used in publishing attempts, so the media must be hosted on a publicly accessible server at the time of the attempt' (Instagram) and 'We will cURL your image/video using the URL provided so it must be on a public server' (Threads). Instagram images: JPEG only ('Extended JPEG formats such as MPO and JPS are not supported'), max 8 MB, aspect 4:5–1.91:1, width 320–1440 px, sRGB; reels: MP4/MOV with moov atom at front, H264/HEVC, AAC ≤48 kHz, 23–60 fps, max 300 MB for reels, 3 s–15 min. Threads: JPEG or PNG, 8 MB images, 1 GB video, MP4/MOV, ≤300 s, width 320–1440. Rate limits: Instagram 100 API-published posts per rolling 24 h (carousel = 1; check GET /{ig-id}/content_publishing_limit); Threads 250 posts per 24 h. Containers expire if not published within 24 h (error 2207020/2207008). Poll GET /{container}?fields=status_code (EXPIRED, ERROR, FINISHED, IN_PROGRESS, PUBLISHED) 'once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes'; Threads recommends waiting ~30 s before publishing. REDIRECTS: Meta's official docs do NOT state a redirect rule. Community evidence: n8n community thread dated 2025-08-11 reports Google Drive links stopped working with error 'Media download has failed. The media URI doesn't meet our requirements.' and summarises Meta's requirements as 'Direct URL to the raw file', 'No redirects or authentication tokens', 'Proper media headers (e.g., video/mp4, image/jpeg)'; a 2026-07-28 dev.to write-up says verify final status 200, Content-Type image/jpeg|image/png, no 301; postpeer error catalogue says 2207052 ('The media could not be fetched from this uri' — official text VERIFIED on Meta error-codes page) is triggered by non-200, wrong Content-Type or zero-byte responses and 2207003 ('It takes too long to download the media') by slow hosts/oversize files. Treat 'HTTP 200, no 3xx, correct image/* or video/* Content-Type, Content-Length present, no auth' as the requirement. A 2026-09-10 Threads post documents that 2207052 'Media download has failed' can be a transient flake that succeeds on retry with a fresh URL — implement retry. TikTok (VERIFIED Media Transfer Guide): PULL_FROM_URL requires the developer app to have verified ownership of the domain (DNS record) or URL prefix (https://host/path/ exactly, via a signature file), otherwise 403 url_ownership_unverified; 'The media URL must use https and should not redirect to another URL'; 'Redirections are not followed. URLs that return HTTP 3xx are considered invalid'; 'The URL must remain accessible for the entire duration of the download process, which times out one hour after the download task is initiated'; video max 4 GB, MP4/WebM/MOV; FILE_UPLOAD chunks 5–64 MB (last up to 128 MB), ≤1000 chunks, sequential; unaudited clients: 'All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode' / can only post to private accounts. Because URL-prefix verification is per-app and per-prefix, PULL_FROM_URL is only realistic with the self-hosted relay or a user bucket whose prefix the Crier *user* verifies in their own TikTok developer app — for a BYO-keys FOSS app FILE_UPLOAD (direct chunked upload, no public URL) is the sane TikTok default. DELETION TIMING: Neither Meta doc says the file must remain available after publishing and no doc says when the fetch happens; the Threads community post states the download happens 'when the container is created', and Instagram's status_code FINISHED means media is ingested. Safe rule for Crier: keep the file until the container reports FINISHED (images are usually FINISHED immediately; videos after processing), then media_publish, then delete; keep a 24 h lifecycle rule as backstop. For TikTok keep until publish status PUBLISH_COMPLETE (up to 1 h).
recommendation: Implement a `MediaHost` plugin interface with a reachability self-test (HEAD/GET the resulting URL from the device: expect 200, no 3xx, Content-Type image/jpeg|image/png|video/mp4, Content-Length > 0) and ship these providers in this priority order: (1) 'Crier Relay' on Cloudflare Workers + R2 — recommended default for power users and the ONLY free route that also satisfies TikTok PULL_FROM_URL (clean https prefix the user can verify, no redirects, exact Content-Type, token-protected PUT/DELETE, lifecycle auto-expiry); publish the Worker in the repo with a one-click deploy. (2) Generic S3-compatible bucket (AWS/R2/B2/MinIO) with client-side SigV4 via `aws_signature_v4` (official Amplify package, has presign + S3ServiceConfiguration unsigned payload) or the unofficial `minio` package; require public-read bucket and store Content-Type on PUT; B2 has the best free tier without a card, R2 needs a payment method and r2.dev is dev-only (use a custom domain). (3) Nextcloud/WebDAV for self-hosters, but probe the final URL because /s/{token}/download behaviour changed in NC 31/32 (prefer /public.php/dav/files/{token}/ or the 'raw' app). (4) Zero-config fallback: Litterbox (1 GB, time=1h for images / 24h for video, anonymous, auto-expiring; most ToS-defensible since the file is fetched once and disappears) with Uguu (128 MiB, 3 h) as a second choice; show a 'third-party host, read their rules' notice and never make it silent. 0x0.st is attractive (token-based deletion, 512 MiB) but its terms could not be fetched today — verify before enabling. (5) Cloudinary free (unsigned preset, 10 MB image / 100 MB video, delete_by_token within 10 min) and Supabase free (50 MB, project auto-pauses after 1 week idle) as optional account-based providers; both are legitimate but have size/pausing caveats. For TikTok default to FILE_UPLOAD chunked direct upload and offer PULL_FROM_URL only when the user has verified their relay/bucket prefix in their own TikTok app; remind users that unaudited TikTok apps post private-only.
